additionalCoursework:
Coursework must include one Biochemistry course and 2 Upper-level Biology courses. Examples of Upper-level Biology courses include Anatomy/Physiology, Cell Biology, Genetics, Microbiology, and Immunology. These courses should be taken at a baccalaureate granting institution or as courses taken as part of a Masters or PhD program.

A minimum of 30 credit hours of AMCAS designated BCPM coursework with letter grades is required.

In-person classwork is strongly preferred to online classwork. A substantial majority of the coursework needs to be in person. 

For more information on our requirements and recommendations, visit:
https://www.med.unc.edu/md/admissions/how-to-apply/admissions-requirements/

medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The UNC School of Medicine policies address both voluntary and involuntary leaves of absence (LOA). Approval for voluntary LOA may be requested for reasons including personal, medical, research, or graduate studies. Involuntary LOA may be required for administrative or medical reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are over 40 student organizations and interest groups available to our students.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of North Carolina School of Medicine is located near downtown Chapel Hill, a town of 60,000. We are at the western corner of the renowned Research Triangle formed by the cities of Chapel Hill, Durham and Raleigh, which has a growing metropolitan area population of nearly 2,000,000. Chapel Hill and neighboring Carrboro are diverse and inclusive communities, and we have an exciting music and arts scene. Our location on the campus is in the health sciences area, which features the schools of nursing, dentistry, pharmacy, and public health and the UNC Hospital complex. We are across the street from the lovely historic UNC main campus.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The School of Medicine does not offer housing on the Chapel Hill campus. When students are assigned to rotations around the state, apartment-style housing is provided.

medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Life can be stressful while pursuing a graduate or professional degree. The School of Medicine knows this and wants to support you during your time here. As an MD or MD/PhD student, you are eligible for School of Medicine specific counseling support. 

Mental Health & Wellness Program information: https://www.med.unc.edu/wellness/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The UNC School of Medicine has a rich tradition of excellence and care. Our mission is to improve the health and wellbeing of North Carolinians and others whom we serve. We accomplish this by providing leadership and excellence in the interrelated areas of patient care, education, and research. We strive to promote faculty, staff, and learner development in a diverse, respectful environment where our colleagues demonstrate professionalism, enhance learning, and create personal and professional sustainability. We optimize our partnership with the UNC Health System through close collaboration and commitment to service. Our vision is to be the nation's leading public school of medicine. We are ranked 2nd in primary care education among all US schools of medicine and 5th among public peers in NIH research funding. To learn more about our mission, visit https://www.med.unc.edu/about/#mission.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Student Affairs provides tutoring services to students when appropriate and available. Tutors are often third and fourth year students who are on leave of absence for research.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: It is a student’s professional responsibility to attend events where patients, their families, physicians, experts dedicate time to an educational experience

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The curriculum offers an education that reflects our mission. The Foundation Phase, the first year and a half of the curriculum, presents courses in medical science in organ-based courses, including normal structure and function as well as the pathophysiology of disease.  Presentation is through interactive large-group sessions, problem-based and case-based small-group sessions, laboratory sessions, and electronic resource materials. Introduction to the profession of medicine begins in the first week of the first year through Patient Centered Care (PCC). PCC provides weekly small-group seminars and experience with both simulated and actual patients. A second weekly seminar, Professional Development, focuses on health care issues.  In addition, students in the Foundation Phase spend a week in each of the three semesters in a primary care private practice. 

The Applications Phase engages students from approximately the middle of their second year to the middle of their third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: UNC is ranked first in the nation for primary care by US News and World Report. Our curriculum features experience in community practices across the entire state in all four years; numerous well-developed service experiences in North Carolina and abroad; a required rotation in Family Medicine, which students rank as one of the best clerkships; and an innovative MD/MPH program, which up to a quarter of students complete. There are also many opportunities for student research in primary care and population health in Family Medicine and Medicine. The state of North Carolina is nationally known for innovation in primary care and community networks, and our Family Medicine, Medicine, and Pediatrics faculty have played leadership roles in this effort. Finally, we have collaborated with North Carolina Blue Cross and Blue Shield to create the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Family Medicine Scholars Program, an innovative program to train future leaders in primary care and the health of the public.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: UNC abounds with opportunities for research as medical students. Our well established MD PHD links 10 outstanding students per year with productive researchers across the full spectrum of disciplines, and our MD PhD students have the highest rate of independent funding for their PhD projects in the country. Our innovative MD MPH program gives interested students training in clinical epidemiology and population health, and up to a quarter of each class enroll. In addition to these formal programs, there are numerous other opportunities and a student research society. Almost 80% of students participate in some type of research experiences while at UNC, and most of these publish papers.

medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The mission of the UNC SOM is to improve the health and well-being of North Carolinians and others whom we serve. We will accomplish this by achieving excellence and providing leadership in the interrelated areas of patient care, education, and research.

Our school’s mission informs the structure and content of our curriculum. Our curriculum reflects the ever-changing practice of medicine, meets the desire for early career differentiation and exploration, and promotes social justice as a cornerstone for equitable and safe healthcare.

Our school’s mission impacts student life and support services. Our student support bench is extensive to promote learning in a respectful and diverse environment.
 
We have an Advisory College system which provides a more accessible social and educational structure in the context of a large student body. 

Our Wellness Program includes group discussions surrounding stress, coping, loss, and more. One-on-one counseling, with therapists, provide services dedicated to medical students and increases access for our students. 

UNC SOM has a multipronged strategy to optimize the Learning Environment including enhanced reporting structures, robust incident management, bystander training, and intentional culture change.
 
Students arrive to medical school at varying points developmentally in their professional identity formation. The Student Professionalism Committee assures that students are educated and held to the highest standards of professionalism by addressing professionalism issues with an eye towards education and support rather than disciplinary action.
 
The Office of Academic Excellence (OAE) provides academic support for students across all training sites around the state. The OAE’s goal is to enable students from all backgrounds to be academically successful in medical school and prepared to pursue the careers of their choosing.

Our school’s mission influences admissions practices and priorities. To care for and represent our state and our nation, the UNC SOM recruits students from a variety of lived experiences to create a socially responsible highly skilled workforce. We not only wish to recruit primary care doctors and individuals who wish to practice in rural communities, but also recruit individuals who will be leaders in academia, science, and industry. We believe that interaction between students with varying clinical, research, and education interests enhances the experience of students at the UNC SOM. Particular programs that help us achieve our goals are described below.

The Community Health Track is a partnership that has grown from the pre-existing accelerated FIRST Program and the Kenan Rural Scholars Program. Leadership from FIRST and Kenan recognized the opportunity for collaboration and the creation of a dedicated track experience for students with shared interests, including rural and underserved care, commitment to the state of North Carolina, and the desire to work within Primary Care.  

The UNC MD-PhD Program prepares high-achieving students to be leaders in academic medicine and scientific health discovery. The primary goal of the MD-PhD Program is to train physician-scientists, fully capable of bridging the gap between science and clinical medicine. 

The Medical Educational Development program (MED) is a summer pipeline program for aspiring medical and dental students.

Our school’s mission is reflected in the professional activities of our graduates. After graduation, our students train in competitive residency programs at top institutions across our state and country ( https://www.med.unc.edu/ome/studentaffairs/residency-and-the-match/residency-placements/ ). Beyond residency, we are proud to see our graduates joining the faculty of top academic centers, as well as successfully practicing clinical medicine.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks. Acceptance form must be completed and deposit paid.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
You should begin requesting your letters of recommendation in early spring, well in advance, of the AMCAS submission verification deadline in June. This will give your professors, advisors, and mentors enough time to compose and submit their letters. LORs from faculty and organizations must be on their letterhead and signed. We begin our interviewing season in September, so to ensure that your applicant profile is complete by the time the season begins, our deadline for submission of the required letters to AMCAS is August 31. However, we do understand that our timeline may not coincide with your school’s Pre-Health Committee, and that is fine. 
Just know, until your required letters are sent to AMCAS, your applicant profile will not be considered complete. Please remember that it is your responsibility to make sure that you designate the UNC School of Medicine as one of the schools to receive your letters.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Online Coursework and P/F Grading 

On-line courses will only be considered if your institution is unable to offer you a place in a seated class, or if the course is offered as a hybrid (in-person and online). We recommend contacting our Admissions office for confirmation of acceptability.

P/F Grading

We require letter grades for any current and future coursework after spring 2021.

CASPer and AMCAS Professional Readiness Exams

We do not require the CASPer exam, or the AMCAS Professional Readiness Exam (formerly known as the AAMC Situational Judgement Test)

Letters of Recommendation

Letters of recommendation from faculty and organizations must be on their letterhead and signed. Requirements and deadlines can be found at: https://www.med.unc.edu/admit/requirements/admissions-process/#step-three--garner-your-letters-of-recommendation-

Admissions Policies
https://www.med.unc.edu/admit/requirements/admissions-process/#step-three--garner-your-letters-of-recommendation-
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
We consider the most recent valid scores. For more information regarding MCATs, please visit: https://www.med.unc.edu/admit/requirements/academic-requirements/

We will consider scores from tests taken between January through September 2024. The latest MCAT score we can consider for this application cycle will be September 12, 2026.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: The minimum criteria can be found at https://www.med.unc.edu/admit/requirements/academic-requirements/
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: If you do not meet the minimum GPA requirements, we require that you either enroll in a post-baccalaureate or science graduate program, in the natural sciences, and complete at least 30 credit hours or more before applying. This gives you the opportunity to show an improvement in your academic ability, and to prepare for graduate level coursework, and will enable us to consider and evaluate your success in the program. Remember, the goal is to demonstrate proficiency in the natural sciences, and only having a few credit hours of post-grad work on your AMCAS application will not give us the evidence that we need. Make sure that you receive a letter-grade for your course work, and not P/F, or medical schools will not be able to determine the GPA improvement, as P/F grades will not be calculated in your post-baccalaureate or graduate GPAs. https://www.med.unc.edu/admit/requirements/admissions-process/
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: If a prospective student is enrolled in "early college" or taking college courses online while in high school, and transferring to a four-year institution, these courses count toward the four-year degree. Please review the UNC School of Medicine Required courses on our website at: https://www.med.unc.edu/admit/requirements/academic-requirements/
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We do not accept updates to your AMCAS application or your supplemental application post-submission. This includes letters of intent, information about a new job, or a publication. Please note, if you are retaking the MCAT, you will need to update your AMCAS application with the next exam date. The Office of Admissions and the Committee on Admissions will use the information provided on the AMCAS application you submitted. If we require additional information, we will contact you.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The Medical Education Development (MED) Program is an intensive educational experience and challenging opportunity to gain insight into the realities of attending medical or dental school.

The MED Program was established in 1974 and is designed to increase opportunities in the health professions for individuals who demonstrate educational promise and commitment to a health career but who have lacked opportunities in the past in moving toward their professional goals. The MED Program is sponsored by the University of North Carolina Schools of Medicine and Adams School of Dentistry, and the State of North Carolina. The program offers a structured summer curriculum at the level of professional education to increase the ability of advanced pre-professional candidates to compete successfully for admission to health professional schools.

medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Only first year UNC School of Medicine students are eligible to apply for the Community Health Training Program.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq:
Application to the Community Health Training Program is only open to current MS1s at UNC School of Medicine.

Selection to the Community Health Training Program will include a review of the application and first semester medical school grades.  Placement to the Accelerated (3-year) MD pathway is subject to availability among GME partners.

https://www.med.unc.edu/md/admissions/how-to-apply/admissions-requirements/
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is a five-year limit on prerequisite coursework. We begin calculating the elapsed time from the YEAR you graduated from the given program.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Committee on Admissions evaluates the qualifications of all applicants and will select the candidates with the greatest potential for accomplishment in one of the many careers open to medical school graduates. The selection factors considered are: a rigorous and successful academic record, competitive MCAT scores, commitment to service, research experience, healthcare experience, extracurricular activities, life and work experiences, letters of recommendation, and communication skills.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is a great opportunity to observe how a physician cares for his or her own patients. We strongly advise that applicants to engage in longitudinal direct-patient contact (one-on-one care) within a health care setting. This is considered a very desirable experience, and necessary, to demonstrate your understanding of patient care, your awareness of the medical profession, and what it takes to become a physician.
